name: Complex Multi-Topic Agent Tests
description: Tests for complex agents with multiple topics, FSM patterns, action chaining, and advanced features

tests.prompt: Build a real estate agent that helps home buyers search for properties, schedule tours, and get mortgage pre-qualification info. The agent should support searching by city, price range, and number of bedrooms. Use a verification gate for mortgage-related info since it requires identity verification. Include a Data Cloud retriever action to assess buyer readiness based on their profile. Actions: Search_Properties (flow://RealEstate_Search), Schedule_Tour (flow://RealEstate_ScheduleTour), Get_Prequalification (apex://MortgageService.getPrequalification), Assess_Buyer (retriever://BuyerReadinessRetriever).
assertions: [fsm:hub-and-spoke] Uses hub-and-spoke pattern with central router directing to specialized topics
[fsm:verification-gate] Verification required before mortgage/prequalification topics
[fsm:no-orphan-topics] All topics reachable from start_agent routing
[fsm:no-dead-ends] All topics have exit paths (transition back to router or escalation)
[fsm:name-collision] start_agent name differs from all topic names
[fsm:router-instructions] start_agent routes based on intent, does not answer directly
[actions:level1-definition] Home search action has inputs for city, price_min, price_max, bedrooms
[actions:numeric-types] Price and bedroom inputs use object type with complex_data_type_name: Number
[actions:output-capture] Search results captured to variables for display
[logic:after-reasoning] Uses after_reasoning for deterministic post-search routing
[logic:conditional-flow] Conditional logic based on search results count
[structure:linked-vars] Has all required linked variables for Service Agent
[safety:ai-disclosure] Identifies as AI real estate assistant, not licensed realtor
[safety:professional-referral] Defers to licensed agents for legal/contract questions

tests.prompt: Create a customer support agent that handles orders, technical support, and billing inquiries. Each domain should have its own topic with specialized actions. The agent should maintain conversation context across turns and route based on user intent. Actions: Get_Order (flow://Support_GetOrder), Create_Ticket (flow://Support_CreateTicket), Get_Invoice (flow://Billing_GetInvoice), Process_Payment (apex://BillingService.processPayment).
assertions: [fsm:hub-and-spoke] Central router with three specialized domain topics
[fsm:router-instructions] Start agent routes based on keywords, does not answer directly
[fsm:no-orphan-topics] Orders, tech support, and billing topics all reachable
[fsm:no-dead-ends] Each domain topic can transition back to router or escalate
[actions:level1-definition] Each topic has domain-specific actions with proper targets
[actions:level2-invocation] Actions properly invoked with with/set parameter bindings
[logic:post-action-top] Post-action state checks at top of procedural instructions (->)
[logic:state-transitions] Clear state transitions between topics based on user intent
[instructions:procedural-mode] Uses -> mode for conditional action-result handling
[instructions:context-aware] Instructions reference collected variables across the conversation
[chat:topic-routing] Clear routing logic with intent keywords for each domain
[chat:context-awareness] Variables persist across topic transitions
[structure:variables-block] Mutable variables for order_id, ticket_id, invoice_id

tests.prompt: Build a case management agent that: 1) verifies customer identity (email + phone), 2) looks up existing open cases for the customer, 3) creates new cases if needed with subject and description, 4) routes complex cases to specialists. Use after_reasoning to chain case creation after collecting all required fields. Actions: Verify_Customer (apex://CaseService.verifyCustomer), Get_Open_Cases (flow://Case_GetOpenCases), Create_Case (apex://CaseService.createCase), Route_To_Specialist (flow://Case_RouteToSpecialist).
assertions: [fsm:verification-gate] Identity verification required before case access
[fsm:linear-flow] Follows logical flow: verify -> lookup -> create/route
[fsm:no-dead-ends] All paths lead to resolution, new case, or escalation
[logic:after-reasoning] Uses after_reasoning to create case after all fields collected
[logic:post-action-top] Post-creation check transitions to confirmation or specialist topic
[logic:conditional-flow] Branches based on: verified?, has_open_cases?, case_created?
[actions:slot-filling] Case subject and description collected via conversational slot-filling (...)
[actions:available-when] Case creation/lookup actions gated by verification_status variable
[actions:output-capture] Captures case_id and case_list from action outputs
[actions:level2-invocation] Proper @actions.X invocation with with/set clauses
[instructions:context-aware] Instructions adapt based on open case count and verification state
[structure:variables-block] Mutable variables for verification_status, case_subject, case_description, case_id

tests.prompt: Build a restaurant reservation agent with 3 topics: table booking, menu inquiry, and dietary accommodations. Each topic has backend actions: Book_Table (flow://Restaurant_BookTable with party_size as integer, date as text, time as text), Get_Menu (apex://MenuService.getMenu with category as text), Check_Dietary (apex://MenuService.checkDietary with dish_name as text, allergy as text). The agent should always use the backend actions to look up real data rather than guessing.
assertions: [fsm:hub-and-spoke] Uses hub-and-spoke routing with central topic selector
[actions:level1-definition] All 3 actions defined with correct targets and I/O types
[actions:level2-invocation] Actions invoked with proper with/set bindings
[instructions:action-aware] Each action topic's instructions reference its actions by purpose — not just describe the topic goal
[instructions:anti-hallucination] Instructions direct the LLM to use actions for data lookup, not fabricate menu items or availability
[safety:ai-disclosure] Identifies as AI reservation assistant
negative_assertions: [instructions:no-ambiguity] Action topic instructions do NOT use passive phrases like 'you can use the action if needed' without directing the LLM to actually call it

tests.prompt: Build a bank customer service agent with 3 topics: account balance, transfer funds, and card services (report lost/stolen, request new card). Actions: Get_Balance (flow://Bank_GetBalance with account_id as text), Transfer_Funds (apex://BankService.transferFunds with from_account as text, to_account as text, amount as integer), Report_Lost_Card (flow://Bank_ReportLostCard with card_last_four as text). The start_agent router must handle cases where users ask about multiple things in one message, e.g. 'Check my balance and also transfer $200 to savings'.
assertions: [fsm:hub-and-spoke] Uses hub-and-spoke routing for 3 service topics
[fsm:router-instructions] Start agent routes based on intent, does not answer directly
[instructions:multi-intent] Start agent instructions include guidance for multi-intent messages — route to first topic, remind about second after completion
[actions:level1-definition] All 3 actions defined with correct flow:// and apex:// targets
[instructions:action-aware] Action topics reference their backend actions in instructions
[safety:ai-disclosure] Identifies as AI banking assistant

tests.prompt: Build an inventory lookup agent for a hardware store with 2 topics: product search and stock check. Actions: Search_Products (apex://InventoryService.searchProducts with query as text, category as text), Check_Stock (apex://InventoryService.checkStock with product_id as text, store_location as text). The agent MUST call the backend actions to get real inventory data. It must NEVER make up product names, prices, or stock counts. If the action returns no results, the agent should say so honestly rather than guessing.
assertions: [actions:level1-definition] Both actions defined with apex:// targets and correct I/O
[actions:level2-invocation] Actions invoked with with/set parameter bindings
[instructions:action-aware] Both topic instructions explicitly reference their search/stock actions as the source of truth
[instructions:anti-hallucination] Instructions explicitly forbid fabricating product data, prices, or availability — must use action results
[instructions:context-aware] Instructions handle the no-results case honestly (tell user, don't invent data)
[safety:ai-disclosure] Identifies as AI inventory assistant
[safety:honest-limitations] Acknowledges limitations when data is not available
negative_assertions: [instructions:no-ambiguity] Instructions do NOT use vague phrases like 'help the user find products' without directing LLM to call the search action
